Overall verdict: needs_changes. The implementer’s Repo/Env/Project declaration is correct, and I saw no forbidden command shapes in their `target_context.commands_run`.

FINDING (high, correctness): The upgrade status is produced as `upgrade-status.json` but is not loaded or rendered by the dashboard, so the required always-shown Tools & Setup / Health row is not actually exposed. Evidence: `dashboard.py:930-944` writes the sidecar, but `dashboard/core.js:253-307` has no `upgrade-status.json` loader, `health-logic.js:45-52` renders only existing health sections, and `capabilities.js:14-17` renders only `state.capabilities`. Recommendation: add `upgradeStatus` to dashboard state loading and render it in the Tools & Setup and/or Health page with tests for up-to-date, pending, behind, last-acknowledged, and absent-marker states.

FINDING (medium, test_coverage): The new tests validate the Python projection/provider but not the dashboard consumer path. Evidence: `test_upgrade_dashboard_f008.py:139-330` calls `upgrade_status_projection`, `provide_upgrade_actions`, and `oc.aggregate`, but no test calls `dashboard.build`, `core.js`, `renderHealthHTML`, or `renderCapabilityCenterHTML`; `rg` found no dashboard JS references to `upgrade-status`/`upgradeStatus`. Recommendation: add build-output and JS rendering tests that prove the row appears from `state/upgrade-status.json`.
